messages:
sam: Quick note — new peregrine-int4 microbatch canary shows intermittent funcall NDJSON merges in streaming. Low rate but reproducible on mixed-length traffic. Anyone tracking this?
anu: Yep, saw a small spike after the int4 kernel tweak. Repro snippet:
```bash
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CANARY' -d '{\"model\":\"peregrine-int4-canary\",\"input\":\"call_tool: meta(doc)->{id:int,tag:string}\"}' https://canary.api.redwood/run
```
Partial stream sample:
{"chunk":"{\"id\":1,\"tag\":\"alpha\",\n"}
{"chunk":"}"}
{"chunk":"{\"id\":2,\"tag\":\"beta\"}\n"}
(there's a `}\n{` boundary without delimiter)
rachel: Sounds like streaming fragments from two requests concatenated. Likely micro-batching + retry overlap. Int4 tokenization shifts make EOS land differently so fragments split oddly.
qa-joe: Our rescue heuristics hide the scale. We should avoid broad fixes. Suggest canary-only sentinel envelope and additional logging first.
infra-bot: Deployed peregrine-int4-canary rev r2026-int4-12 to infra/canary at 2026-03-23T09:20:00Z
sam: Plan: (1) enable envelope sentinel for canary clients only, (2) add per-fragment request_nonce in trace headers, (3) run 8h A/B: sentinel vs control. Collect parse_ok, fragment_count, last_token_hex, retry_count.
anu: I'll roll the sentinel flag and extra trace fields. Keep heuristics disabled but log rescued cases as alerts.
rachel: If sentinel shows lots of cross-request joins, next step is strengthening the streaming transport to always flush a delimiter between request streams. That might be a safe short-term guardrail.
qa-joe: Kicking off 10k-call canary runs at 2026-03-24T00:00Z. Will post metrics here.
sam: Thanks. If anyone sees spikes in production, ping this thread and we can toggle the feature-flag off quickly. 🙂
